newsitem.title: GERMANY: German banks agree to pay full sick-pay - union.
newsitem.headline: German banks agree to pay full sick-pay - union.

text.p: German banks have agreed to resume paying 100 percent sick pay until a definitive wage agreement is struck with unions, a spokeswoman for the HBV union said on Monday.
The spokeswoman said the rule, agreed at a meeting between banks and unions in Frankfurt, would apply immediately to the 460,000 employees in the sector.

She added that the issue of possible compensation would be discussed at a future meeting, not yet scheduled. Talks about compensation could take place on January 21 and 22 next year when regular wage talks are set to begin, union sources said.
The banking sector in November became the only major German sector in which employers got together to apply a new law allowing sick pay to be cut to 80 percent of normal pay from 100 percent.

Before the talks began, union leaders had warned that there would be protests across the sector as early as this week if banks did not back down from the cuts. Last month more than 15,000 German bank employees took to the streets to protest.
